item.title: Future Scholars in Business and Society: Current Work and Emerging Directions
item.content:encoded:
Barrie Litzky, Drexel University

This special issue of Business and Society Review is exclusively for doctoral students and seeks to showcase emerging scholarship examining the relationship between business and society. The initiative emphasizes developmental support alongside rigorous peer review, recognizing that doctoral research operates at varying stages of completion and methodological advancement.

The special issue welcomes both empirical and conceptual contributions addressing core topics in business ethics, corporate responsibility, stakeholder relations, sustainability, social innovation, and governance. Manuscripts need not conform to standard journal article length and may present abbreviated, developmental, or complete projects. All submissions will undergo the journal's standard double-blind review process.

Three manuscript development workshops are offered throughout 2026 to strengthen submissions, featuring feedback from senior scholars and peer dialogue opportunities. While participation in a workshop is encouraged, it is not required for manuscript submission.

Appel publié par Business and Society Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical decision-making and moral responsibility
  • Stakeholder theory and value creation
  • Inequality, justice, and organizational impacts
  • Sustainability and social innovation
  • Technology, AI, and data ethics
  • Corporate governance and responsibility
  • Business-government relations and policy
  • Institutional and global perspectives
  • Conceptual and methodological advancements
  • Pedagogical research in business ethics

item.title: Past Accomplishments and Future Challenges within Supply Chain Management Research
item.content:encoded:
Jessica L. Darby, Auburn University

Rebekah (Bekki) Brau, Brigham Young University

David J. Ketchen, Auburn University

This annual special issue invites authors to submit proposals for integrative literature reviews of important supply chain management research streams. The special issue aims to synthesize current knowledge and provide direction for future development in the field. Rather than submitting full papers, authors propose a review project that outlines how they will examine and synthesize a focused area of SCM scholarship.

Proposals are evaluated on their significance, feasibility, potential breadth of interest, clarity, and contribution to future research directions. The review should address a notable gap in existing literature or provide substantial new perspective beyond prior reviews. The guest editors emphasize that proposals must be carefully crafted and authors should seek colleague feedback before submission, as rough drafts will not be pre-screened.

Appel publié par Journal of Business Logistics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Integrative reviews of supply chain management research that focus on a specific topic or apply a particular theory across different topics
  • Research streams in supply chain management that require scholarly review
  • Significant SCM research areas with limited recent published reviews or novel contributions beyond existing reviews
  • Supply chain management topics of broad interest across specialty areas and neighboring fields

Timeline

  • Invalid DateTime: Issue will be published
  • August 1, 2026: Submission window for proposals
  • October 1, 2026: Decisions on proposals will be provided
  • March 1, 2027: Full papers due
  • June 1, 2027: Feedback to authors on full papers
  • September 1, 2027: Revised papers due
